name: import, the case that was found
why: A statement pattern without `;` matches the statement with its `;`. 0.2.0 replaced the `;` too (calls ~644, 647, 753, 757 of the review).
source:
import { a } from "./x";
import { b } from "./y";
expected:
import { a } from "./z";
import { b } from "./y";

name: import, `;` in the pattern and the rewrite
why: The pattern names the `;`: it is part of the match and of the replacement. Nothing is left over.

name: import, `;` only in the rewrite
why: The rewrite ends in what the match has after the pattern: it is replaced along, so no `;;`.

name: import without `;` (ASI style)
why: Nothing after the pattern: nothing to keep.

name: import, other spacing than the pattern
why: The pattern's text is followed through the match with whitespace left aside.

name: import of nothing: an empty `$$$` hole last
why: A hole for many that matched nothing has no place in the match; the pattern is followed as if it were not there.

name: default import, a hole in the middle
why: The pattern ends in literal text after its last hole.

name: return, the pattern ends in a hole
why: Where the pattern ends is where its last hole ended in the match.

name: return, a comment before the `;`
why: Everything after the pattern stays: the comment with the `;`.

name: return, a line comment after the `;`
why: A comment after the statement is not part of the match at all.

name: return with an anonymous hole `$_`
why: ast-grep does not say where an anonymous hole matched; nux names it ($NUXANON0) for the search, so that it does.

name: two anonymous holes still match different things
why: Each anonymous hole gets a name of its own: they do not have to match the same text, as with `$_`.

name: const declaration
why: A declaration is a statement with its `;`.

name: export const
why: The same, inside an export.

name: throw
why: Another statement.

name: a call: an expression, not a statement
why: The match is the call without the `;`, as before. Nothing changes here.

name: several statements on one line
why: Only the matched statement changes; the `;` of each stays where it was.

name: a rewrite into two statements
why: The kept `;` ends the last of them; the rewrite writes the `;` between them itself.

name: deleting a statement
why: A rewrite to '' deletes the whole statement, its `;` included: leaving a lone `;` is never what is wanted.

name: deleting a call leaves its `;` (ast-grep's match, unchanged)
why: The match of an expression has no `;`, so a lone `;` stays, as in 0.2.0. To delete the statement, put the `;` in the pattern (next case).

name: deleting a call with `;` in the pattern
why: With the `;` in the pattern, the match is the statement.

name: JavaScript
why: The same grammar family as TypeScript.

name: TSX
why: And with JSX.

name: Rust let
why: Rust statements end in `;` too.

name: Rust use
why: A declaration with its `;`.

name: Rust expression
why: An expression inside a statement: no `;` in the match.

name: C return
why: C statements.

name: Java return
why: Java statements.

name: Python: no terminators
why: Nothing after the pattern in a language without `;`.

name: Go: no terminators
why: The same in Go.
